deed: Doron Almog founded a rehabilitation village in the Negev named after his son Eran
title: Doron Almog founded a rehabilitation village in the Negev named after his son Eran, which today also has a rehabilitation hospital

trailer.text: Doron Almog, who was head of the IDF's Southern Command, gained renown as the first Israeli paratrooper reconnaissance commander to land at the rescue mission in Entebbe in 1976.
His son Eran, born in 1984, never spoke and never made eye contact.
While searching for suitable care for him, Doron and Didi Almog helped the organization ADI expand its mission.
The rehabilitation village they founded in the Negev is called Nahalat Eran, in memory of Eran, who lost his battle with Castleman's disease in 2007, at the age of 23.
According to the organization's website, the village today cares for nearly 400 residents and special education students, and in June 2022 a rehabilitation hospital opened there.

glance.label: Scale
glance.value: Nearly 400 residents and students, according to the website

stations.title: Before: a fallen brother, a son who did not speak

paragraphs.text: Doron Almog's brother, Eran Avrutsky, fell in the Yom Kippur War as commander of a tank unit defending the Golan Heights.
According to the Jewish Journal, he was shot in the left leg and bled for seven days before dying of his injury.
Almog said he swore to stay in the military and never leave a wounded soldier behind.
In 1976 he was the first Israeli paratrooper reconnaissance commander to land at the rescue mission in Entebbe.
From 2000 to 2003 he was head of the IDF's Southern Command, and protected the southern border from infiltration by terrorists from Gaza.
In 1984 a son was born to Doron and Didi Almog, and he was named Eran, after his uncle.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the baby was born profoundly disabled, lacking fibers connecting the two halves of the brain.
According to the Jewish Journal, he was diagnosed with an intellectual disability and autism at the age of 8 months.
According to ADI, Doron Almog battled the status quo for years to secure the best possible care for his son.

stations.title: The idea: a village for a lifetime

paragraphs.text: Almog said they visualized a village for the full lifespan of children like Eran, and began planning it in 2000.
While searching for suitable care for Eran, Doron and Didi Almog fell in love with the organization ADI and helped it expand its mission.
According to ynet, they undertook to develop and grow the community, so that their son could live with people facing similar challenges.
The ALEH network, within which the Negev village was established, was founded in 1982 by parents who needed a solution for their severely disabled children.
Almog said the village was established with the specific aim of breaking with conventions.
He said the village would not have been built if not for Eran.
According to him, Eran became the greatest teacher of his life and taught him to see the person and not the disability.

stations.title: The land, the construction and the name

paragraphs.text: According to the Jerusalem Post, the village was built on land donated by the Israel Lands Authority.
In June 2003 the cornerstone-laying ceremony was held. Prime Minister Ariel Sharon spoke at it, and Yair Lapid, then a media personality, served as master of ceremonies.
According to Maariv, the first phase was inaugurated in 2006.
According to the Jerusalem Post, Eran was the first person to move into ALEH Negev, when construction was completed in January 2006.
In 2007 Eran lost his battle with Castleman's disease, at the age of 23.
In February 2007, the Jerusalem Post reported that the organization was seriously considering naming the village after him.
After his death, the village's name was changed to ALEH Negev-Nahalat Eran.
After Eran's death, Almog stayed on to continue his son's legacy.
Almog said his son's spirit had spread to every corner of the village.
According to the organization's website, the village cares for and empowers nearly 400 residents and special education students with severe disabilities.
According to the Jerusalem Post (2014), about 80% of the annual operating budget, NIS 30 million, comes from the government, and the rest from donations, foundations and partners.
According to Maariv, Liza Edni came to the village four years ago, following an offer to help establish an agricultural farm.
On the farm she established, people without disabilities and people with moderate disabilities work together.
According to the Jerusalem Post, about 40 prisoners are escorted to the village to volunteer with residents one-on-one.
In 2011 the prisoners' volunteer program won the Israel Prison Service an Offender Management and Reintegration Award from the International Corrections and Prisons Association.
At the village, an Orthodox Jewish teenager, a high-school student, met an Arab preschool child; according to the article, in most places in Israel the two would never have met.
The mother of Liam, a child with autism, said he has been at the village for a third year and receives the best treatments.
The brother of Daniel Hagari, the former IDF Spokesperson, lives in the village and was Eran Almog's roommate.
According to ynet, for ten years more than 1,000 visitors from Israel and around the world came to the village every month.

stations.title: A rehabilitation hospital for the south

paragraphs.text: According to a ynet report from the COVID-19 period, before the rehabilitation hospital in the village opened, Israel, with a population of 9 million, had only 850 dedicated rehabilitation beds, and only 50 of them were in the south.
According to the Jerusalem Post (2018), Almog was raising funds for a hospital costing 50 million dollars, which would serve many residents of the Negev.
According to the Jewish Journal (2018), he had recently raised $23 million, and funds were still needed to build housing for students, employees and families.

According to the Times of Israel, the Harvey and Gloria Kaylie Rehabilitation Medical Center was inaugurated on 12 April 2022 with Prime Minister Bennett attending; according to the organization's website, it opened in June 2022.
According to the organization's website, it is the first and only dedicated rehabilitation hospital in southern Israel.

According to a ynet report written before the hospital opened, the new hospital was planned to include 108 rehabilitation beds, with a research center alongside it in partnership with Ben Gurion University.

According to Almog, in an article from the coronavirus period, before the rehabilitation hospital was completed, at least 100 civilians and soldiers from the Negev received rehabilitative treatments in the village every day, through the health funds and the Ministry of Defense.
According to the website, after October 7 the center treated dozens of war-wounded IDF soldiers and civilians.
Sergeant Roi, a soldier wounded in Lebanon, said he underwent a total of 12 surgeries following the injury.
According to him, a friend gave him the phone number of a doctor at ADI Negev, and after the conversation he was invited to continue his rehabilitation there.

stations.title: Acceptance and inclusion beyond the village

paragraphs.text: Almog worked with the Ministry of Education to create an experiential education program that would deliver messages of acceptance and inclusion to all Israeli youth.
According to ADI, the 'Tikkun Olam' program exposed hundreds of thousands of Israeli students to peers with disabilities.
Almog said that in the past there was a stigma in Israel about having children with disabilities.
According to the Jerusalem Post, he speaks openly about his son's disabilities and is sharply critical of Israel's lack of inclusion of people with disabilities.

According to the Jerusalem Post (2014), following his experience at the village, Prime Minister Netanyahu asked him to direct the Headquarters for the Economic and Community Development of the Negev Bedouin.
According to ADI, construction will later begin on 'Merhavei Daniel', a township of 500 families adjacent to the village, which will integrate residents with disabilities.
In May 2016 Doron Almog was awarded the Israel Prize for lifetime achievement and contribution to society and the state.
According to ADI, the prize committee chose him for leading a revolution in the care of Israel's most vulnerable population, and for a change in societal perception of people with disabilities.
According to eJP, the organization marked its 20th anniversary.
President Herzog said at the celebrations that the village had sparked a true revolution in the world of welfare services.
Almog is Chairman of the Executive of the Jewish Agency for Israel, and still serves as Chairman of ADI Negev-Nahalat Eran.

claims.text: רועי סיפר שחבר נתן לו את מספר הטלפון של רופא בעדי נגב, ולאחר השיחה הוזמן להמשיך שם את שיקומו.
claims.quote: חבר נתן לו את מספר הטלפון של רופא בעדי נגב, ולאחר השיחה הוזמן לעבור במקום את המשך השיקום

claims.text: אלמוג פעל עם משרד החינוך ליצירת תוכנית חינוך חווייתית שתעביר מסרים של קבלה והכלה לכלל הנוער בישראל.
claims.quote: Doron worked with the Ministry of Education to create an experiential education program that would deliver the same positive messages to all Israeli youth

claims.text: לפי ADI, תוכנית 'תיקון עולם' חשפה מאות אלפי תלמידים ישראלים לבני גילם עם מוגבלות.
claims.quote: exposing hundreds of thousands of Israeli students of every age to peers with disabilities

claims.text: אלמוג אמר שבעבר היה בישראל סטיגמה כלפי הולדת ילדים עם מוגבלות.
claims.quote: In the past, there was a stigma in Israel about having children with disabilities, Almog says.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, אלמוג פתוח לגבי מוגבלותו של בנו וביקורתי בחריפות על היעדר ההכלה של אנשים עם מוגבלות בישראל.
claims.quote: has been open about his own son's disabilities and sharply critical of Israel's lack of inclusion for the disabled

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט (2014), בעקבות ניסיונו בכפר ביקש ממנו ראש הממשלה נתניהו לנהל את המטה לפיתוח כלכלי וקהילתי של הבדואים בנגב.
claims.quote: Almog was asked by Prime Minister Binyamin Netanyahu two years ago to direct the Headquarters for the Economic and Community Development of the Negev Beduin.

claims.text: לפי ADI, בהמשך תחל הקמת 'מרחבי דניאל', יישוב של 500 משפחות הסמוך לכפר שישלב דיירים עם מוגבלות.
claims.quote: ADI Negev-Nahalat Eran will begin the construction of Merhavei Daniel, a 500-family township adjacent to the village

claims.text: לפי ADI, ועדת פרס ישראל בחרה באלמוג על שהוביל מהפכה בטיפול באוכלוסייה הפגיעה ביותר בישראל ועל שינוי בתפיסה החברתית כלפי אנשים עם מוגבלות.
claims.quote: leading a revolution to advance the caring of Israel’s most vulnerable population and bringing about a crucial change in societal perception of individuals with disabilities

claims.text: לפי eJP, הארגון ציין את יום השנה ה-20 שלו.
claims.quote: Last Wednesday, the organization marked its 20th anniversary

claims.text: הנשיא הרצוג אמר בחגיגות שהכפר הצית מהפכה אמיתית בעולם שירותי הרווחה.
claims.quote: this village has sparked a true revolution in the world of welfare services.

claims.text: אלמוג הוא יו"ר הנהלת הסוכנות היהודית לישראל ועדיין משמש יו"ר ADI נגב-נחלת ערן.
claims.quote: Now the Chairman of the Executive of the Jewish Agency for Israel, Doron Almog still serves as the Chairman of ADI Negev-Nahalat Eran

claims.text: לפי ג'ואיש ג'ורנל (2018), אלמוג ייסד את הכפר ב-2004 והוא משתרע על 40 דונם אמריקאי ומשרת למעלה מ-700 ילדים.
claims.quote: Founded by Almog in 2004, the village sits on 40 acres and supplies more than 700 children throughout Israel

claims.text: לפי eJP, דורון ודידי אלמוג ייסדו את ADI נגב-נחלת ערן ב-2005.
claims.quote: In 2005, Doron and Didi Almog founded ADI Negev-Nahalat Eran.

claims.text: לפי נתוני הכפר שהובאו במעריב, מתגוררים בו כיום 274 דיירים.
claims.quote: על פי נתוני הכפר, כיום מתגוררים בו 274 דיירים

claims.text: לפי eJP, הארגון מעסיק 850 איש, מאכלס 170 דיירים קבועים עם מוגבלות ומשרת יותר מ-3,000 איש בשנה.
claims.quote: now employing 850 people and housing 170 permanent residents with disabilities. It serves more than 3,000 people a year

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט (2018), בכפר ALEH נגב 150 דיירים, מבוגרים וילדים עם מוגבלויות קשות.
claims.quote: ALEH Negev has 150 residents, both adults and children with severe disabilities.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט (2014), הכפר נבנה לקיבולת של 250 איש ומאכלס 140 דיירים.
claims.quote: The innovative rehabilitative village, built with a 250-person capacity, now houses 140 residents

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט (2018), בכפר 380 עובדים, מהם יותר מ-100 עובדים סביב השעון בבתי המגורים.
claims.quote: There are 380 employees at the village including more than 100 who work around the clock in the residential homes.

claims.text: לפי JNS, בישראל יש פחות מ-850 מיטות בית חולים שיקומיות, ואף אחת מהן לא באזור הדרום.
claims.quote: there are fewer than 850 rehabilitative hospital beds in the entire country—none of them in Israel’s southern region

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט (2018), ציפו להשלים את בית החולים ב-2020.
claims.quote: They expect to break ground in a few months and hope to complete the hospital in 2020.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט (2018), 10,000 תלמידים השתתפו בתוכניות המודעות, והמארגנים קיוו להגיע ל-100,000.
claims.quote: So far 10,000 students have participated in these programs and the organizers hope to reach 100,000 in the next few years.

claims.text: לפי ADI, ערן נקרא על שם דודו שהושאר לדמם בשדה הקרב במלחמת יום כיפור, והוא נולד עם אוטיזם ברמה גבוהה ולקויות התפתחותיות קשות.
claims.quote: Eran, named for his uncle who was left to bleed to death on the battlefield during the Yom Kippur War, was born with high-level autism and severe developmental disabilities.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, אחרי ויכוח ארוך על המשך הדרך בחרו אלמוג ואשתו בחיים.
claims.quote: He and his wife initially had a long debate about if and how to go on, and ultimately chose life.

claims.text: בג'רוזלם פוסט נכתב בפברואר 2007 כי הארגון שוקל ברצינות לשנות את שם הכפר החדש על שם בנו המנוח של אלמוג.
claims.quote: Organization is seriously considering renaming its newly built Negev village after the deceased son of Maj.-Gen. (res.) Doron Almog.

claims.text: רשת עלה, שהכפר בנגב קם במסגרתה, הוקמה ב-1982 על ידי הורים שחיפשו פתרון לילדיהם עם מוגבלות קשה.
claims.quote: ALEH was founded in 1982 by parents who needed a solution for their severely disabled children.
claims.checker_note: audit: quote found on the fetched page

claims.text: ב-2011 זיכתה תוכנית ההתנדבות של האסירים את שירות בתי הסוהר בפרס על ניהול ושילוב מחדש של עבריינים, מטעם האיגוד הבינלאומי לשירותי כליאה ובתי סוהר (International Corrections and Prisons Association).
claims.quote: an Offender Management and Reintegration Award in 2011 from the International Corrections and Prisons Association
claims.checker_note: audit: quote found on the fetched page

claims.text: טיימס אוף ישראל (12.4.2022): בית החולים נפתח באותו יום, בנוכחות ראש הממשלה בנט

quote_translations.c34: ADI Negev - Nahalat Eran would not have been built if not for Eran, our son. The child who never spoke and never made eye contact.
quote_translations.c35: According to him, Eran taught him "to see the person and not the disability"
quote_translations.c32: 23 years ago the cornerstone was laid for the first buildings, and in 2006 the first phase was inaugurated
quote_translations.c40: Four years ago she came to ADI Negev following an offer to help establish an agricultural farm at the site
quote_translations.c36: Edni established in the village an integrative agricultural farm where people without disabilities and people with moderate-level disabilities work together
quote_translations.c39: Liam has been in the village for a third year already. He receives the best treatments there are and we love the staff
quote_translations.c37: They performed a few more surgeries on me there, and in total I underwent 12 surgeries following the injury
quote_translations.c38: A friend gave him the phone number of a doctor at ADI Negev, and after the conversation he was invited to undergo the rest of his rehabilitation there
quote_translations.c33: According to village data, 274 residents live there today
